#!/bin/bash
set -e

WORK_DIR="/tmp/bench72183367"
K="$WORK_DIR/bin/k"
REG_HOST="127.0.0.1:15183"
NS="default"

# the credentials of the registry: what an engineer would do with 'docker login', but as a Kubernetes Secret, which is what
# the kubelet hands to CRI-O when it pulls (CRI-O does not read Kubernetes Secrets itself)
. <(sed 's/^/CRED_/' "$WORK_DIR/registry.cred")

echo "[solution] creating the Secret regcred (type kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson) with the credentials of $REG_HOST in namespace $NS..."
"$K" -n "$NS" delete secret regcred --ignore-not-found >/dev/null
"$K" -n "$NS" create secret docker-registry regcred \
    --docker-server="$REG_HOST" --docker-username="$CRED_username" --docker-password="$CRED_password"

echo "[solution] imagePullSecrets of a pod cannot be changed once it exists: recreating the pod app with the Secret..."
"$K" -n "$NS" delete pod app --wait=true --ignore-not-found >/dev/null
{ cat "$WORK_DIR/pod.yaml"; printf '  imagePullSecrets:\n  - name: regcred\n'; } | "$K" apply -f - >/dev/null

echo "[solution] waiting for the pod app to run..."
for _ in $(seq 1 40); do
    [ "$("$K" -n "$NS" get pod app -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}' 2>/dev/null)" = "Running" ] && break
    sleep 2
done
"$K" -n "$NS" get pod app

#!/bin/bash
# the Secret goes to the default ServiceAccount (the pods created afterwards get it injected), then the pod is recreated from the unchanged pod.yaml
set -e
W=/tmp/bench72183367
K=$W/bin/k
NODE_CRICTL=$W/bin/node-crictl
REG=127.0.0.1:15183
. <(sed 's/^/C_/' $W/registry.cred)    # C_username, C_password
WAIT_APP() { for _ in $(seq 1 20); do [ "$($K -n "${1:-default}" get pod app -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}' 2>/dev/null)" = Running ] && break; sleep 2; done; }
$K create secret docker-registry regcred --docker-server=$REG --docker-username="$C_username" --docker-password="$C_password"
$K patch serviceaccount default -p '{"imagePullSecrets":[{"name":"regcred"}]}'
$K delete pod app --wait=true >/dev/null
$K apply -f $W/pod.yaml >/dev/null
WAIT_APP

#!/bin/bash
# the config.json an engineer would get from docker login, written by hand and stored as a Secret of type kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson
set -e
W=/tmp/bench72183367
K=$W/bin/k
NODE_CRICTL=$W/bin/node-crictl
REG=127.0.0.1:15183
. <(sed 's/^/C_/' $W/registry.cred)    # C_username, C_password
WAIT_APP() { for _ in $(seq 1 20); do [ "$($K -n "${1:-default}" get pod app -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}' 2>/dev/null)" = Running ] && break; sleep 2; done; }
AUTH=$(printf '%s:%s' "$C_username" "$C_password" | base64 -w0)
printf '{"auths":{"%s":{"auth":"%s"}}}\n' "$REG" "$AUTH" > $W/dockerconfig.json
$K create secret generic regcred --type=kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson --from-file=.dockerconfigjson=$W/dockerconfig.json
rm -f $W/dockerconfig.json
$K delete pod app --wait=true --ignore-not-found >/dev/null
{ cat $W/pod.yaml; printf '  imagePullSecrets:\n  - name: regcred\n'; } | $K apply -f - >/dev/null
WAIT_APP

#!/bin/bash
# the image is pulled on the node by hand with crictl pull --creds (what the kubelet would do), the pod has no Secret: it runs from the node's store, nothing is configured for other pods
set -e
W=/tmp/bench72183367
K=$W/bin/k
NODE_CRICTL=$W/bin/node-crictl
REG=127.0.0.1:15183
. <(sed 's/^/C_/' $W/registry.cred)    # C_username, C_password
WAIT_APP() { for _ in $(seq 1 20); do [ "$($K -n "${1:-default}" get pod app -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}' 2>/dev/null)" = Running ] && break; sleep 2; done; }
$NODE_CRICTL pull --creds "$C_username:$C_password" $REG/bench72183367/secure/app:1.0
$K delete pod app --wait=true --ignore-not-found >/dev/null
$K apply -f $W/pod.yaml >/dev/null
WAIT_APP

#!/bin/bash
# a node-wide auth file for containers/image (the substitute of docker login): the pod runs without any Secret
set -e
W=/tmp/bench72183367
K=$W/bin/k
NODE_CRICTL=$W/bin/node-crictl
REG=127.0.0.1:15183
. <(sed 's/^/C_/' $W/registry.cred)    # C_username, C_password
WAIT_APP() { for _ in $(seq 1 20); do [ "$($K -n "${1:-default}" get pod app -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}' 2>/dev/null)" = Running ] && break; sleep 2; done; }
AUTH=$(printf '%s:%s' "$C_username" "$C_password" | base64 -w0)
sudo mkdir -p /run/containers/0
printf '{"auths":{"%s":{"auth":"%s"}}}\n' "$REG" "$AUTH" | sudo tee /run/containers/0/auth.json >/dev/null
$K delete pod app --wait=true --ignore-not-found >/dev/null
$K apply -f $W/pod.yaml >/dev/null
WAIT_APP
